headline: No school changed tier this run. Tripwires unchanged. The AAU v. DHS hearing before Judge Kobick was scheduled for today, 6 Nov 2026, 3pm US Eastern — still no ruling found as of this run (18:10 UTC / 1:10pm ET, before the hearing time).

tripwires.name: DHS SEVIS Help Hub CPT page
tripwires.detail: Re-confirmed 6 Nov 18:10 UTC via direct fetch — unchanged: "Last updated: August 24, 2026," links the two August broadcast messages by name, no lawsuit mention.

tripwires.name: Tufts I-Center CPT page
tripwires.detail: Re-confirmed 6 Nov 18:10 UTC via direct fetch — unchanged, still carries "the I-Center is unable to process CPT requests for non-required internships at this time"; no new language on already-authorised students.

tripwires.name: Federal Register rulemaking on CPT
tripwires.detail: DHS's own CPT-guidance tripwire page re-confirmed unchanged 6 Nov 18:10 UTC via direct fetch — SEVP "plans to release draft guidance that clarifies previous CPT-focused guidance documents," still no date. Lawsuit: Association of American Universities et al. v. DHS, No. 1:26-cv-14520 (D. Mass.); the preliminary-injunction/stay-of-agency-action hearing before Judge Kobick was scheduled for today, 6 Nov 2026, 3pm US Eastern — this run's search (18:10 UTC / 1:10pm ET, before the hearing) found no ruling yet. CPT remains guidance, not a rule.

tripwires.name: Retroactive cancellation spreading
tripwires.detail: Still tripped, re-checked 6 Nov 18:10 UTC — no school newly moved into 'cancels' this run. Davidson, MIT, Skidmore and University of South Florida remain the only confirmed interruptions of already-granted CPT.

tiers.label: Already-approved CPT stopped or withdrawn
tiers.sub: The most severe response: students who already held an authorisation were told to stop work, or had it withdrawn.

schools.name: Davidson
schools.note: 15 Aug — paused new CPT and cancelled approved Fall 2026 authorisations after consulting counsel

schools.name: MIT
schools.note: paused new, incl. Professional Practice Requirement internships; contacting already-approved Fall 2026 students about alternatives

schools.name: Skidmore

context: First CPT-specific litigation: on 5 Oct a coalition (AAU, Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, NAFSA, AICUM) sued DHS in federal court in Massachusetts over the Aug 12/24 BCMs, calling them procedurally invalid and impermissibly retroactive, with an emergency injunction motion filed the same night seeking to block enforcement while the case proceeds; case is Association of American Universities et al. v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security et al., No. 1:26-cv-14520 (D. Mass.); pending, no ruling yet (NAFSA held a member town hall on the case 7 Oct). A hearing on the plaintiffs' preliminary-injunction/stay-of-agency-action motions is set for 6 Nov 2026, per Carnegie Mellon's own OIE litigation-update page and independently corroborated on the University of Oklahoma's own ISS page. No third broadcast message. DHS's stated position: 'nothing about these regulations has changed.' ICE is auditing schools, with SEVP decertification as the stated risk. Immigration attorneys flag a retroactive-scrutiny risk — past CPT revisited at the OPT, STEM-OPT or H-1B stage. The common institutional reading of the new standard: integral to the curriculum, required of all students in the programme for degree completion, a documented cooperative agreement with the employer, and DSO authorisation before training begins.
